To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
senescence of cucumber cotyledons triggered a temporal increase in the density of inactive PS II centers and a decrease in the density of active PSII centers.
the senescence of Cucumissativus cotyledons triggers the formation of heat sink PS II centres, which are non-functional due to the absence of QA.
senescence of cucumber cotyledons triggered a conversion of QA-reduction centers to non- QA reducing centers (heat sink).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of fast Chl a transients for probing the senescence-induced structural and functional changes in the PS II of Cucumissatius cotyledons.
probing the senescence-induced alteration in the structure and photofuntions of PS II using Chl a fluorescence O-J-I-p transients.
understanding the molecular and biochemical basis of senescence-induced changes in photosynthetic apparatus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

senescence-induced changes in the photosynthetic apparatus of cotyledons, as probed in the present work by fast O-J-I- P transients, is a result of a combination of several factors, namely: (i), senescence-induced conversion of active PS II centers to non- active centers; (ii), clustering of active and inactive PS II centers; and (iii), senescence induced changes in the electron acceptor side of PS II.

senescence of Cucumus cotyledons induced a decrease in the density of active PSII reaction centres, a decrease in the apparent trapping efficiency of PS II, a decrease in intersystem PQ pool and an increase in the density of heat sink PS II reaction centres.

the fast Chl fluorescence induction O-J-P transient, when analysed with equations of JIP test, is a powerful tool for probing senescence driven structural and photofunctional alterations in PS II of plant leaves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, senescence-induced heterogeneity in PSII centers affects QA<-->QB acceptor side electron equilibrium.
the senescence induced alterations of the photosynthetic machinery in the chloroplasts are reflected as changes in the fast Chl fluorescence O-J-I- P transient.
the JIP-test is a useful tool to probe the senescence-induced changes in photosynthetic machinery in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the fast Chl fluorescence O-J-I- P transients, with time resolution of at-least 50 mircoseconds and use of the JIP-test, provides a valuable, non invasive, rapid biophysical probe for studying the senescence process in plants in terms detecting photosynthetic activity and heterogeneity of different type of PS II units.
the JIP-test is a valuable, non-destructive tool to probe the biophysical and functional alterations in photosynthetic units of plants under stress conditions.
senescence-induced changes in the structure and function of PS II can be probed by the fast O-J-I fluorescence transient.
